PREP-01.title: Investigation Preparation and Planning
PREP-01.description: Defines the investigation objectives, scope, roles, target systems, and procedures in advance, and secures the required legal authority and resources. Use this category when a paper's primary contribution concerns investigation design, legal or organizational preparation, resource allocation, or standard operating procedures rather than an evidence-analysis algorithm. Listed terms and cases are non-exhaustive examples; research making substantive contributions to adjacent technologies may relate to multiple categories.

description.definition: Designing investigation scope, targets, resources, evidence-processing order, and reporting based on the objectives and issues of a case
indicators: Defining investigation scope and scenarios
Allocating roles, tools, staff, and priorities
insufficient_alone: Only performing technical analysis of individual evidence
Planning a literature review, experiment, publication study, or general research project rather than a digital investigation

description.definition: Securing and confirming the legal basis and permitted scope for accessing, collecting, and examining digital evidence
indicators: Securing a warrant, consent, or other authority
Defining jurisdiction and permitted collection scope
insufficient_alone: Only evaluating admissibility after collection

IDEC-01.title: Identification of Potential Digital Evidence Sources
IDEC-01.description: Identifies devices, accounts, networks, and remote services that may hold case-related evidence to define the scope and priority of preservation and collection. It includes discovering user accounts, authentication traces, relationships, and cloud touchpoints as well as physical devices. Analysis of acquired content and prioritization of evidence are more directly related to examination and triage, respectively. Listed terms and cases are non-exhaustive examples; research making substantive contributions to adjacent technologies may relate to multiple categories.

IDEC-01-01.title: On-scene Search and Digital Device Detection

description.definition: Searches for PCs, mobile devices, storage media, CCTV, IoT, wearables, and mobility equipment at a scene
indicators: Searching a scene for digital devices
Recording device state, connectivity, and context
insufficient_alone: Acquiring or examining data inside an already discovered device without searching for and documenting potential digital evidence sources at the scene

description.definition: Identifies network assets, access paths, accounts, and authentication traces linked to the target
indicators: Discovering network topology, assets, and services
Identifying endpoints, accounts, and access paths
insufficient_alone: Analyzing acquired packets or logs without identifying network assets, access paths, accounts, or endpoints

IDEC-02.title: Digital Evidence Triage
IDEC-02.description: Prioritizes examination under limited time and resources by assessing relevance, volatility, remote-deletion risk, accessibility, and analysis cost. The defining task is deciding which devices and data should be preserved, collected, or examined first during initial response. Work that performs acquisition or detailed content analysis is more directly related to the corresponding category. Listed terms and cases are non-exhaustive examples; research making substantive contributions to adjacent technologies may relate to multiple categories.

description.definition: Prioritizes the seizure and examination of PCs, phones, servers, CCTV, and IoT devices according to relevance, power state, encryption, volatility, and remote-deletion risk
indicators: Prioritizing device-importance scoring and decisions based on live state
Prioritizing volatility and remote-deletion risk
insufficient_alone: Prioritizing files or logs within one device without comparing the seizure or examination priority of physical devices

PRCP-01.title: Evidence State Preservation
PRCP-01.description: Records and controls the state, environment, access, communications, and write operations of target devices and data before collection to reduce alteration, damage, or loss. It covers scene preservation, isolation, signal blocking, write protection, and third-party preservation requests. Actual acquisition and post-collection retention or chain-of-custody management may be more directly related to adjacent categories. Listed terms and cases are non-exhaustive examples; research making substantive contributions to adjacent technologies may relate to multiple categories.

description.definition: Restricts and records physical and logical access by people and processes to target devices and media at the scene
indicators: Controlling and recording scene control and evidence identification
Controlling and recording restriction of user or process access
insufficient_alone: Blocking communications without controlling and recording human or process access to the device at the scene

description.definition: Isolates a live system from networks or external interaction while accounting for volatile data and encryption state, limiting remote manipulation and data changes
indicators: Isolating a live system from networks
Balancing isolation with volatile-data preservation
insufficient_alone: Blocking writes to storage without isolating a live system from networks or remote interaction

description.definition: Uses airplane mode, shielding, and hardware or software write blockers to prevent remote signals and minimize changes to original media
indicators: Blocking Faraday shielding and wireless blocking
Blocking USB or SATA write blockers and verification that source media were not altered
insufficient_alone: Network-isolation strategy or forensic-image format work without blocking signals or writes to the original device or medium

description.definition: Requests account freezes, log preservation, or litigation holds from service providers or custodians
indicators: Requesting preservation orders or requests, account freezes
Requesting provider log retention and emergency preservation of foreign or cloud evidence
insufficient_alone: Downloading already preserved data without requesting an account freeze, log hold, or third-party preservation

COLL-01.title: Device Data Collection
COLL-01.description: Acquires data from storage media and digital devices through physical or logical methods while minimizing changes and recording collection and integrity information. It includes acquisition from storage, mobile, IoT, and other devices, with emphasis on acquisition scope, accuracy, and reproducibility. Data in transit or held by remote services is more directly related to network and cloud collection. Listed terms and cases are non-exhaustive examples; research making substantive contributions to adjacent technologies may relate to multiple categories.

description.definition: Prioritizes volatile memory, communications, location and authentication records, and system or application logs according to relevance, volatility, and collection cost
indicators: Prioritizing selective acquisition and volatile-first collection
Prioritizing relevance-based acquisition strategies
insufficient_alone: Prioritizing physical devices without selecting data inside a device by relevance, volatility, or collection cost

description.definition: Creates a bit-for-bit copy of storage media, including allocated and unallocated space,
indicators: Acquiring disk imaging, bit-stream copying and chip-off
Acquiring JTAG, low-level acquisition and preservation of unallocated space
insufficient_alone: Acquiring only files, folders, backups, or API-visible data without copying raw sectors and unallocated space

description.definition: Uses operating-system or application interfaces to collect selected files, folders, databases, logical volumes, and associated metadata
indicators: Acquiring selected files, folders, or databases
Collecting backups, exports, or API-visible data
insufficient_alone: Copying all raw sectors without acquiring selected data through an operating-system or application interface
Creating or receiving a volatile-memory dump without acquiring selected persistent files, folders, databases, backups, exports, or logical volumes
Downloading, opening, loading, or receiving sample files or a research corpus only as experimental input, without implementing or studying an evidence-acquisition procedure

COLL-02.title: Network and Cloud Data Collection
COLL-02.description: Acquires packets, logs, accounts, and service data from networks, open online sources, anonymous networks, and cloud services in a lawful and reproducible manner. It includes methods for acquiring evidence from remote or distributed environments, preserving collection-time state, and handling protocol, API, and provider dependencies. Interpretation of acquired material is more directly related to the matching examination category. Listed terms and cases are non-exhaustive examples; research making substantive contributions to adjacent technologies may relate to multiple categories.

description.definition: Captures wired or wireless traffic or collects device, system, application, router, firewall, and server logs through local agents, exports, or remote transmission
indicators: Capturing packets, flows, or syslog
Collecting firewall, DNS, or proxy logs with timestamps
Continuously collecting and preserving device, system, or application logs
Transmitting collected logs to a remote forensic or monitoring server
insufficient_alone: Analyzing previously provided traffic or logs without implementing or performing their collection
Using, resampling, augmenting, or generating a synthetic or benchmark network dataset without capturing traffic or logs from a network, device, application, or logging source

description.definition: Directly retrieves, crawls, downloads, or archives posts, accounts, metadata, advisories, vulnerability records, threat knowledge, malware samples, documents, and other research or evidentiary records from lawfully accessible websites, repositories, search engines, social media, and public databases
indicators: Crawling public websites and social media
Archiving public data with collection-time evidence
Retrieving vulnerability, weakness, attack-pattern, defensive-control, or threat-advisory records from public repositories for analysis
Actively gathering malware samples, documents, software, or other records from multiple public repositories to construct or maintain the paper's analysis corpus
insufficient_alone: Analyzing relationships or credibility in existing OSINT without collecting public-source data
Using a prepackaged public dataset without retrieving, selecting, or integrating public-source records
Receiving a corpus from a third party or citing its public origin without the authors performing a public-source collection step

COLL-02-03.title: Anonymous Network and Dark Web Data Collection

description.definition: Collects sites, posts, and transaction data from Tor and other anonymous or dark-web services while preserving access paths, timestamps, and collection context
indicators: Crawling Tor services, markets, or forums
Preserving volatile dark-web content and context
insufficient_alone: Attributing actors or transactions in existing dark-web data without collecting and preserving anonymous-service content

description.definition: Acquires cloud and SaaS logs, objects, volume snapshots, account activity, and endpoint caches through APIs, exports, and synchronization records
indicators: Acquiring CSP APIs, SaaS exports and snapshots
Acquiring object versions, audit logs and synchronized endpoint caches

Using authenticated APIs, exports, or synchronization to retrieve hosted social, messaging, collaboration, storage, or other SaaS account data, posts, messages, feeds, notifications, activity, or metadata
insufficient_alone: Analyzing already acquired cloud records without API-, export-, snapshot-, or synchronization-based acquisition

COLL-03.title: Forensic Image Creation
COLL-03.description: Stores acquired data as a forensic image with source structure, metadata, acquisition details, and hashes to support later integrity verification and reproduction. It includes image creation, evidence-format design, compression, splitting, metadata preservation, and tool interoperability. Acquisition mechanics and later hash comparison are more directly related to acquisition and integrity verification, respectively. Listed terms and cases are non-exhaustive examples; research making substantive contributions to adjacent technologies may relate to multiple categories.

description.definition: Stores data, acquisition metadata, and hashes in raw, E01, AFF, or similar forensic formats
indicators: Designing or analyzing headers, segments, and metadata structures in E01/EWF, AFF
Storing evidence with acquisition information and hashes
insufficient_alone: Reading data from a medium without defining or examining a forensic container that stores evidence, acquisition metadata, and integrity values

PSCP-01.title: Evidence Storage and Chain of Custody
PSCP-01.description: Continuously records the receipt, transfer, packaging, transport, access, storage, and disposal of evidence so that its identity and integrity can be demonstrated. It includes chain of custody, evidence lifecycle, transfer and access auditing, and long-term preservation policy. The focus is post-collection continuity rather than scene preservation or analytical algorithms. Listed terms and cases are non-exhaustive examples; research making substantive contributions to adjacent technologies may relate to multiple categories.

description.definition: Compares cryptographic hashes calculated at collection and later stages and checks image or file consistency to detect changes
indicators: Verifying hashes, digital signatures and Merkle trees
Verifying blockchain-backed integrity records
insufficient_alone: Detecting content forgery without comparing integrity values across collection and later processing stages

PSCP-01-02.title: Physical Storage Environment and Media Management

description.definition: Protects evidence media from temperature, humidity, shock, and electromagnetic effects and manages seals, access controls, logs, and backups
indicators: Managing evidence-vault design, seals and access control
Managing environmental monitoring, media degradation
insufficient_alone: Managing logical permissions or retention schedules without controlling media storage, seals, environment, or degradation

PSCP-01-03.title: Retention Period and Legal Requirement Management

description.definition: Manages retention periods, access permissions, and return or deletion conditions according to applicable law, warrants, policy, and case status
indicators: Managing retention schedules, legal holds and return or deletion after case closure
Managing data-minimization retention and jurisdiction-specific obligations
insufficient_alone: Requesting emergency third-party preservation without managing retention, return, or deletion requirements

description.definition: Irrecoverably deletes evidence and copies or destroys media through an approved process after retention duties end, recording the target, method, and time
indicators: Applying secure deletion, crypto-erasure, or degaussing
Verifying and recording physical destruction
insufficient_alone: Recovering incident-deleted data without securely deleting or destroying evidence after retention duties end

EXAM-01.title: Forensic Data Preprocessing
EXAM-01.description: Normalizes and indexes heterogeneous data and reduces duplicate or irrelevant material to prepare it for consistent search and correlation. It includes pre-parsing preparation, common-schema transformation, indexing, deduplication, and relevance filtering. The focus is enabling downstream analysis rather than acquiring sources or interpreting event meaning. Listed terms and cases are non-exhaustive examples; research making substantive contributions to adjacent technologies may relate to multiple categories.

description.definition: Converts times, identifiers, fields, and encodings from diverse investigative files, logs, and databases into common forms and builds searchable indexes
indicators: Mapping heterogeneous fields and schemas
Normalizing timestamps and building search indexes
insufficient_alone: Interpreting an existing chronology without normalizing heterogeneous times, identifiers, fields, or encodings

Generic machine-learning feature scaling, vectorization, tokenization, embedding, or train-test preprocessing without normalizing heterogeneous investigative evidence sources or building a forensic search index

description.definition: Uses hash sets, file types, time ranges, keywords, and case relevance to exclude known, duplicate, or irrelevant data and select evidence for priority review
indicators: Filtering known files, duplicates, and hash matches
Selecting by keyword, time, type, or relevance
Applying regex, keyword lists, or suspicious-event rules to a forensic timeline or evidence collection and returning only matched case records
insufficient_alone: Prioritizing physical devices without filtering duplicate, known, irrelevant, or out-of-scope data
Screening or excluding publications in a literature review, or generic experimental preprocessing and train-test selection not performed on investigative evidence or case data

EXAM-02.title: Virtualization and Container Forensics
EXAM-02.description: Examines images, configurations, logs, and execution traces from hypervisors, virtual machines, and containers to determine state and activity in virtual environments. It includes analysis of layers, snapshots, volatile workloads, and host-guest relationships specific to virtual environments. Ordinary operating-system or cloud-service logs are more directly related to their corresponding categories. Listed terms and cases are non-exhaustive examples; research making substantive contributions to adjacent technologies may relate to multiple categories.

description.definition: Examines virtual disks, snapshots, hypervisor logs, memory, and network traces to determine virtual-machine configuration, execution state, and user activity
indicators: Examining VMware, Hyper-V and KVM
Examining VMDK, VHD and QCOW
insufficient_alone: Examining only a trusted execution environment without virtual-machine configuration, state, or activity artifacts

description.definition: Examines container images and layers, runtime configuration, orchestration logs, and volatile workloads
indicators: Examining container images, layers, and filesystems
Analyzing runtime, pod, namespace, and orchestration logs
insufficient_alone: Analyzing cloud account logs without examining container images, layers, runtime state, or orchestration records

EXAM-03.title: File System and Operating System Forensics
EXAM-03.description: Examines partitions, volumes, file systems, and persistent or volatile operating-system artifacts to reconstruct storage structure, system state, and user activity. It covers system-level traces left by storage layers and operating systems, including file placement, execution, access, and memory state. Application-specific internal data is more directly related to Application Forensics. Listed terms and cases are non-exhaustive examples; research making substantive contributions to adjacent technologies may relate to multiple categories.

description.definition: Analyzes partition tables, volume metadata, logical or encrypted volumes, and unallocated space
indicators: Analyzing MBR, GPT and LVM
Analyzing RAID, APFS containers and encrypted volumes
insufficient_alone: Interpreting file metadata without examining partition tables, volume metadata, encryption layers, or storage layout

description.definition: Analyzes metadata, directories, allocation records, journals, and timestamps in NTFS, APFS, ext, and other file systems
indicators: Analyzing MFT, journals and inodes
Analyzing catalogs, allocation bitmaps and deleted entries
insufficient_alone: Parsing a document or media format without examining filesystem allocation, directory, journal, or timestamp structures

description.definition: Analyzes registry data, event logs, accounts, authentication records, and execution or access traces
indicators: Examining Windows Registry, Event Logs and Prefetch and LNK
Examining macOS plist and Unified Logs and Linux journals
Analyzing operating-system process, system-call, kernel, file-I/O, account, authentication, execution, or access-event traces
insufficient_alone: Analyzing only an application's private database or cache without examining operating-system artifacts

description.definition: Extracts processes, modules, network connections, cryptographic keys, and live data from RAM images to examine operating-system state at acquisition time
indicators: Examining memory forensics, process and kernel-object enumeration
Examining modules, sockets and credentials
insufficient_alone: Extracting one application's sessions or content without examining system-wide processes, kernel objects, or connections

EXAM-04.title: Application and File Forensics
EXAM-04.description: Examines application storage and memory and the internal structures of documents, media, and databases to determine user actions and content meaning. It covers persistent and volatile data created by user applications and the semantic structures of individual file formats. Generic OS artifacts and storage structures are more directly related to File-System and OS Forensics. Listed terms and cases are non-exhaustive examples; research making substantive contributions to adjacent technologies may relate to multiple categories.

description.definition: Directly extracts, parses, or examines application-specific persistent databases, preferences, configurations, caches, histories, logs, and file structures stored by an application on desktop, mobile, cloud-client, vehicle, IoT, or embedded platforms
indicators: Examining browser history, messenger databases and email stores
Examining cloud-client caches, mobile sandboxes
Parsing infotainment, IoT, or embedded-application SQLite databases, settings, logs, caches, and related files
insufficient_alone: Analyzing only memory-resident data without examining the application's persistent storage artifacts
Collecting system or device logs that merely contain application execution events
Processing generic timeline events that mention applications without parsing application-owned storage
Providing a framework capable of collecting arbitrary application data without examining application-specific artifacts
Using or mentioning an application only as part of a research scenario

description.definition: Extracts sessions, inputs, decrypted content, keys, and temporary data from application process memory to examine live application state
indicators: Examining heaps, stacks and session tokens
Examining decrypted messages, in-memory databases
insufficient_alone: Examining only kernel or system-wide memory without extracting state from a specific application process

description.definition: Parses headers, metadata, and internal objects in documents, archives, images, video, and databases to examine content and creation or modification traces
indicators: Parsing internal headers, fields, records and object relationships
Reverse-engineering proprietary storage structures in documents, backups, archives, databases, or media containers
Extracting embedded objects and metadata according to container structure
Interpreting or recovering damaged files from their internal format structures
insufficient_alone: Only viewing or searching file content or browsing files and directories without analyzing an internal storage format

EXAM-05.title: Network and Cloud Forensics
EXAM-05.description: Correlates packets, device logs, open-source information, dark-web data, and cloud records to reconstruct communications, access, account activity, and remote-service actions. It includes deriving behavior and incident context from remote communications and service records. If acquisition is the primary contribution, use the corresponding network or cloud collection category. Listed terms and cases are non-exhaustive examples; research making substantive contributions to adjacent technologies may relate to multiple categories.

description.definition: Correlates captured packets and network-device or server logs over time to analyze sessions, access paths, parties, data movement, and anomalous activity
indicators: Reconstructing protocols, flows, and sessions
Correlating DNS, HTTP, TLS, and server logs
insufficient_alone: Studying packet-capture devices or log acquisition without reconstructing sessions, access paths, or network activity

description.definition: Retrieves for substantive interpretation, validates, filters, links, enriches, queries, or correlates accounts, posts, relationships, metadata, advisories, vulnerabilities, weaknesses, attack patterns, defensive controls, and other records from open websites and public databases
indicators: Linking public accounts to people or entities
Validating posts, locations, relationships, and timelines
Correlating vulnerability, weakness, attack-pattern, defensive-control, and public threat records with assets, events, or incident entities
Constructing or querying CVE-CWE-CAPEC, ATT&CK, IoC, advisory, or defensive-control relations from public sources and applying the resulting links or paths to security analysis

Building and querying a local knowledge base that integrates public vulnerability or threat records and applies their descriptions, severity, weakness, exploit, consequence, or mitigation meaning to individual assessments
Classifying or interpreting public threat-feed, phishing-site, exploit, or advisory records by threat type, campaign behavior, hosting pattern, technique, affected target, or security meaning
insufficient_alone: Developing crawlers or collection preservation without validating or correlating the collected public information
Importing public identifiers as dataset labels or model features without examining, validating, linking, enriching, or interpreting their public-source records
Nearest-neighbor retrieval from a private training corpus when the retrieved records are not public-source intelligence and their threat meaning is not interpreted

EXAM-05-03.title: Anonymous Network and Dark Web Data Examination

description.definition: Analyzes posts, accounts, transactions, and cryptocurrency addresses from anonymous networks and the dark web to link activity patterns with other intelligence or evidence
indicators: Profiling dark-web actors, markets, and forums
Linking aliases, PGP keys, wallets, and activity times
insufficient_alone: Using Tor or the dark web only as a collection channel without examining accounts, posts, transactions, or activity relationships

description.definition: Analyzes cloud logs, objects and versions, volumes, account permissions, and API activity
indicators: Reconstructing cloud audit trails, IAM and object access and sharing
Reconstructing API calls, multi-tenant attribution
Analyzing hosted SaaS account, post, message, feed, notification, deletion, sharing, permission, or API-response behavior after remote acquisition
insufficient_alone: Using cloud acquisition APIs or snapshots without analyzing acquired records for actions, changes, sharing, or relationships

ANYS-01.title: Evidence Correlation and Case Reconstruction
ANYS-01.description: Correlates evidence across time, people, accounts, devices, and content, then analyzes relationships and event order to reconstruct the overall course of an incident. It includes research that fuses multiple analytical results into an incident-level explanation. Cross-source correlation, temporal and relational models, and hypothesis testing are more central than parsing individual files or logs. Listed terms and cases are non-exhaustive examples; research making substantive contributions to adjacent technologies may relate to multiple categories.

description.definition: Uses keywords, similarity, patterns, semantics, and context to find and connect case-relevant documents, messages, media, and other content in large datasets
indicators: Searching content by semantics, similarity, or patterns
Extracting entities and clustering relevant content
Searching a forensic timeline, log corpus, document set, messages, or media with case keywords, regex patterns, semantic queries, or suspicious-event rules to return investigator-relevant records
insufficient_alone: Building a search index without using meaning, similarity, patterns, or context to find case-relevant content

Detecting anomalous nodes, classifying attacks, or extracting CTI entities and relations without searching, selecting, or connecting evidentiary documents, messages, media, or human-readable content for a case

Retrieval-augmented generation, nearest-neighbor lookup, or similarity search used only to improve a prediction model, vulnerability assessment, or research benchmark rather than to find case-relevant evidentiary content

description.definition: Corrects time zones and clock offsets across devices, services, and logs, then places events on a common timeline to analyze sequence and gaps
indicators: Building a cross-source super timeline
Correcting clock skew and timestamp provenance
insufficient_alone: Extracting timestamps from a single artifact without correcting clock differences and integrating events from multiple sources on a common timeline

description.definition: Derives case-, incident-, or security-assessment-relevant explicit links among evidentiary and security entities such as people, accounts, hosts, assets, vulnerabilities, attack patterns, defensive controls, locations, transactions, communications, events, artifacts, and incidents to support case-level correlation, security-assessment correlation, attack-path analysis, or reconstruction
indicators: Linking evidentiary entities through link analysis, knowledge graphs, or entity resolution
Deriving communication, transaction, artifact, identity, or incident relationships for an investigation
Correlating entities across evidence sources to reveal case-relevant connections
Deriving links among event, log, flow, action, or attack-stage records to identify coordinated or multi-stage incident behavior
Correlating host, identity, event, time, or infrastructure records into explicit incident relationships, even when those relationships also support detection
Linking assets, vulnerabilities, weaknesses, attack patterns, controls, and topology, then deriving security relationships or attack paths from those explicit links
Converting measured similarity among malware samples, artifacts, or incidents into explicit links that reveal families, variants, provenance, or coordinated behavior
insufficient_alone: Searching or listing items from a single source without modeling relationships among evidentiary entities

Using graph topology, graph neural networks, message passing, mathematical interaction models, or computational dependencies only as a predictive or optimization method without deriving case-level relationships among evidence, entities, or incidents
A detection objective alone; the method must output, infer, or materially exploit explicit relationships among incident evidence, entities, events, actions, or stages

Describing how components of a generic reference architecture interact, exchange data, or form a workflow without deriving relationships among actual or reviewed security evidence, entities, events, or incidents

description.definition: Combines analyzed events and temporal or causal relationships to derive a multi-step incident sequence, attack path, actions, actors, or circumstances, with optional evaluation of conflicts and uncertainty
indicators: Combining events from multiple sources into an incident sequence linking actions, actors and outcomes
Testing competing hypotheses or possible incident paths against observed evidence
Resolving conflicting records, missing intervals and temporal uncertainty to reconstruct the incident
Integrating analytical findings to explain who performed which actions and how
Deriving a multi-step attack sequence or path from explicitly linked event, host, identity, time, and infrastructure records
Using multi-hop event relations, causal links, or attack-graph paths to infer an incident sequence, even when the underlying records originated from one dataset or collection system
Structurally synthesizing a recurring multi-stage attack lifecycle and mapping actions, observables, or detection features to its successive stages across reviewed studies
insufficient_alone: Only ordering events chronologically or correlating timestamps across sources without reconstructing incident actions, causality, or hypotheses
Using a graph or sequence model only to assign an independent class label without producing or materially reasoning over a multi-step incident path
Naming generic attack phases without deriving, mapping, or structurally synthesizing the actions, observables, and transitions that form a multi-step incident lifecycle

REPT-01.title: Forensic Result Presentation and Reporting
REPT-01.description: Presents analysis through tables, charts, relationship graphs, and timelines and communicates reproducible findings, supporting evidence, and limitations in reports. It includes communicating findings to investigators, courts, and decision-makers in an understandable and verifiable form. Presentation, explainability, reporting standards, and legal use are more central than a new detection algorithm. Listed terms and cases are non-exhaustive examples; research making substantive contributions to adjacent technologies may relate to multiple categories.

description.definition: Visualizes time, location, networks, statistics, and data distributions in charts, timelines, and graphs to clarify complex evidence relationships and key findings
indicators: Visually encoding temporal, identity, device, location, or communication relationships in forensic timelines, link charts, or maps
Developing interfaces for exploration, filtering and drill-down across large evidence collections
Using visual representations to explain conflicting evidence, uncertainty, or analytical provenance
Evaluating visualization support for forensic decisions or expert explanation
Constructing and interpreting relationship-network diagrams whose nodes and edges encode evidentiary samples, entities, similarity, provenance, or incident links
insufficient_alone: Merely presenting ordinary tables, charts, plots, screenshots, model explanations, or rendering an already-derived graph as decoration without using the visual encoding to explore, interpret, or explain forensic evidence relationships

description.definition: Documents the examination purpose, evidence identifiers, tools and procedures, findings, interpretive basis, limitations, and validation information in a structured report
indicators: Structuring a forensic report with evidence identifiers, tools, procedures, findings, interpretive basis and limitations
Linking reported findings to source evidence through provenance and audit trails
Generating reproducible reports from a standard schema or template
Developing reporting methods for expert explanation, review, or legal submission
insufficient_alone: Ordinary paper writing, experimental-result summaries, or log and result-file output without addressing forensic reporting structure or procedure

description.definition: Reviews authority and procedure, relevance, identity, integrity, chain of custody, and analytical reliability
indicators: Reviewing admissibility, authenticity and reliability
Reviewing relevance, chain of custody and legal evaluation criteria for digital evidence
insufficient_alone: Securing collection authority without reviewing evidence identity, integrity, custody, procedure, or analytical reliability
Mentioning legal importance, courtroom use, trust, or evidentiary value without evaluating procedural admissibility criteria

CMNF-01.title: Anti-forensics Countermeasures
CMNF-01.description: Identifies and addresses deletion, damage, encryption, hiding, tampering, and anonymization that obstruct access to or interpretation of evidence. It includes detecting or bypassing forensic-evasion techniques and recovering damaged or protected evidence. The defining concern is obstruction, concealment, or degradation of evidentiary reliability rather than ordinary analysis. Listed terms and cases are non-exhaustive examples; research making substantive contributions to adjacent technologies may relate to multiple categories.

description.definition: Recovers storage components from devices or media damaged by water, impact, or fire and acquires data through a safe interface
indicators: Using chip-off, board repair, or NAND reconstruction
Recovering water-, fire-, or impact-damaged media
insufficient_alone: Recovering logically deleted or corrupt data without handling physically damaged devices or media

description.definition: Recovers access to otherwise unavailable encrypted evidence by applying recovered or cracked credentials, cryptographic weaknesses, or forensic recovery techniques to transform existing ciphertext or locked encrypted content into accessible plaintext data
indicators: Recovering or cracking a key or password and using it to decrypt protected content
Exploiting cryptographic implementation or key-management weaknesses to decrypt data
Decrypting encrypted storage, backups, files, communications, or device content
insufficient_alone: Bypassing only a screen lock or access control without decrypting protected data
Finding a plaintext private key or seed in memory, importing a key into a wallet, or using it to access assets without decrypting ciphertext
Discussing keys, encryption, or memory remnants without applying them to decryption
Encrypting, signing, hashing, or otherwise protecting newly generated data, logs, communications, or storage without decrypting existing ciphertext
Routine authorized reading through the system's intended credentials, keys, access controls, or normal service functionality without recovering otherwise inaccessible encrypted evidence

description.definition: Analyzes screen locks, secure boot, account authentication, access controls, and vendor protections
indicators: Bypassing secure boot, screen locks, or authentication
Defeating hardware, enclave, or vendor protections
insufficient_alone: Decrypting data with an available key without bypassing or defeating an access-control or protection mechanism

description.definition: Detects inconsistencies and patterns left by log deletion, timestamp manipulation, trace wiping, encryption, hiding tools, and other evasion activity
indicators: Detecting inconsistencies and residual traces caused by log wiping, timestomping, or artifact cleaning
Identifying indicators of fileless execution, decoys, or forensic-tool detection
Linking deletion, encryption, or concealment patterns to attempts to obstruct forensic examination
Combining missing, altered and temporally inconsistent artifacts to infer anti-forensic activity
insufficient_alone: Merely observing encrypted, deleted, or hidden data without identifying indicators or intent of forensic evasion
Recovering deleted data without analyzing patterns of deletion or trace removal

description.definition: Uses file-system metadata, unallocated space, journals, backups, and file signatures to restore deleted or logically damaged data
indicators: Carving files and recovering deleted records
Repairing databases and reconstructing fragmented files
Restoring ransomware-encrypted or logically damaged files from protected history, backups, journals, or verified recovery copies
Implementing and exercising rollback or protected-history restoration, including verification that damaged or encrypted files are recoverable
insufficient_alone: Repairing physical media without restoring logically deleted, fragmented, or corrupt data
Creating backups, snapshots, or protected copies without implementing or evaluating a restoration procedure

description.definition: Analyzes hashes, signatures, metadata, encoding properties, and temporal or content inconsistencies to detect editing, forgery, or tampering
indicators: Detecting document, log and database tampering
Detecting provenance inconsistencies and integrity anomalies
Detecting spoofed, replayed, injected, jammed, or falsified system, sensor, control, or telemetry records through content, timing, provenance, or consistency analysis
insufficient_alone: Detecting manipulation only in image or video without examining tampering in documents, logs, databases, or timestamps

description.definition: Detects data concealed through steganography, hidden areas or files, alternate data streams, and abnormal encoding
indicators: Detecting steganography and hidden partitions
Finding slack-space, ADS, or covert-container data
insufficient_alone: Linking an anonymous actor to an identity without detecting hidden data, steganography, or covert storage

description.definition: Correlating pseudonyms, aliases, addresses, and behavioral patterns with auxiliary data
indicators: Linking pseudonyms, aliases, and identities
Correlating browser or network fingerprints
insufficient_alone: Anonymous or pseudonymous data is merely present without an attribution or linkage analysis
Clustering IP addresses, tools, attacks, malware, or campaigns without resolving a pseudonymous account, address, device, or actor to a more specific digital or real-world identity

description.definition: Analyzes calls between a TEE and the operating system, shared memory, remote attestation, and hardware behavior to acquire and verify isolated data and execution flow
indicators: Examining Intel SGX, ARM TrustZone and secure enclaves
Examining confidential computing, remote attestation
insufficient_alone: Examining an ordinary virtual machine without analyzing isolated execution, attestation, shared memory, or hardware protection

CMNF-02.title: Forensic Infrastructure
CMNF-02.description: Provides reference data, common representations, selection, tool validation, readiness, education, and laboratory controls that support efficient, interoperable, and reliable forensics. It includes research that improves quality, repeatability, standardization, and operational capability across forensic practice. Reference data, representation, validation, readiness, education, and facilities are the main subtopics. Listed terms and cases are non-exhaustive examples; research making substantive contributions to adjacent technologies may relate to multiple categories.

description.definition: Builds, integrates, maintains, or distributes reusable standard reference material whose known hashes, signatures, artifacts, forensic images, expected findings, or ground truth are used to identify, compare, filter, or verify evidence and forensic correctness in investigations or validation
indicators: Building or updating known-good and known-malicious hash or signature sets
Creating forensic images, corpora, or samples with explicit ground truth
Publishing and versioning reusable reference corpora for evidence comparison or identification
Integrating standardized forensic ground-truth cases with expected findings for correctness validation
Publishing a documented forensic image, artifact timeline, performed user actions, and machine-comparable expected findings as reusable validation ground truth
Managing provenance, labels, quality and duplication in reference data
insufficient_alone: Using an existing dataset only for training, testing, or performance evaluation without building, maintaining, or improving the reference data itself

Creating one-off experimental samples, controlled scenarios, generated training data, or ground truth only to evaluate another method when the resulting resource is not a substantive reusable deliverable
Normalizing, augmenting, or relabeling an existing benchmark solely for the paper's own model experiment without publishing a reusable reference resource

Building a research benchmark, challenge dataset, or test corpus only to train, rank, or measure a model, algorithm, or tool, without serving as standard reference material for evidence identification, comparison, or forensic correctness

description.definition: Represents investigation-relevant evidence, artifacts, observables, actions, relationships, and provenance in interoperable schemas or serializations for consistent exchange and reuse across tools or organizations
indicators: Representing evidence ontologies, common schemas, and evidence-exchange formats
Mapping domain-specific artifacts or observables into an interoperable standard representation
Representing event-object relationships, provenance, and cross-tool or cross-organization interoperability
insufficient_alone: Examining only a forensic-image container format without a common representation of evidence objects, actions, relationships, or provenance
Using a serialization or schema merely as an incidental input or transport without modeling investigation-relevant artifacts, actions, relationships, observables, or provenance
A model feature vector, internal database schema, message format, ledger record, or fused representation created only for one system without an interoperability or evidence-exchange objective

description.definition: Tests the accuracy, reliability, reproducibility, coverage, error conditions, or version-specific results of a digital-forensic tool, method, procedure, or benchmark using ground truth or repeatable validation procedures
indicators: Comparing forensic-tool output with established ground truth
Testing accuracy and reproducibility across runs, tools, versions, or environments
Measuring false positives, false negatives, error conditions and support limitations
Applying a documented validation protocol and standardized test material

Validating the authors' own forensic method when evidentiary correctness, reliability, repeatability, failure modes, or robustness is a distinct validation objective beyond routine predictive-performance reporting
Conducting a dedicated comparative or adversarial validation of existing forensic methods with common ground truth and repeatable protocols
insufficient_alone: Performing an ordinary performance or accuracy evaluation of a prediction model, sensor algorithm, localization method, IDS, or other non-forensic system
Using a forensic tool in an experiment or case without evaluating the tool itself

Reporting train-test accuracy, benchmark scores, ablation, cross-dataset generalization, or robustness only as routine evaluation of the paper's newly proposed predictor or estimator, without a distinct forensic-correctness validation objective

description.definition: Establishes logging, time synchronization, retention policy, responsibilities, collection points, and response procedures before incidents
indicators: Designing logging, synchronization, and evidence sources
Defining pre-incident retention, roles, and response procedures
insufficient_alone: Collecting evidence after an incident without pre-establishing logging, synchronization, retention, roles, or collection points

description.definition: Defines knowledge, skills, and proficiency by role and manages professional capability through education, practical exercises, assessment, certification, and continuing training
indicators: Developing competency frameworks, curricula and certification
Developing proficiency testing, practical scenarios
insufficient_alone: Testing tool accuracy without defining or assessing role-based forensic knowledge, skills, or proficiency

description.definition: Builds a forensic laboratory with controlled access, network separation, calibrated equipment, work records, and information-security controls for safe evidence handling
indicators: Establishing ISO/IEC 17025-style quality systems, evidence rooms
Establishing access controls, calibration and operating procedures
insufficient_alone: Providing personnel training without establishing laboratory access, equipment, calibration, records, or security controls

CVGF-01.title: Incident Response
CVGF-01.description: Detects and analyzes security incidents, intrusions, malware, ransomware, and threat intelligence, determines attack paths and impact, and supports evidence preservation, response, recovery, and recurrence prevention. It includes deployable or evaluated security detection and analysis whose direct purpose is identifying malicious activity, as well as post-incident forensic investigation and response. Generic prediction, optimization, or sensing research with only an incidental security example is outside scope. Listed terms and cases are non-exhaustive examples; research making substantive contributions to adjacent technologies may relate to multiple categories.

description.definition: Continuously monitors, collects, or analyzes cyber-security events, logs, network or host telemetry, device security telemetry, and compromise indicators to detect intrusions, cyber anomalies, and evolving incidents, with optional time alignment and correlation
indicators: Monitoring and correlating SIEM, endpoint telemetry
Monitoring and correlating anomaly detection, audit logging
Deploying real-time or streaming intrusion detection across edge, fog, cloud, endpoint, or IoT layers
Implementing an online, streaming, or operational IDS procedure and evaluating that procedure with captured, replayed, benchmark, or simulated cyber-security data

Executing software or attacks in a controlled environment, continuously observing runtime behaviors or request state, and driving an automated malware, intrusion, containment, or response decision from that telemetry
Repeatedly observing cyber state or correlated event sequences and driving detection, containment, or response decisions in an implemented or emulated operational loop
Constructing incident state from related events, flows, alerts, or stages to detect an evolving or multi-step attack rather than classifying each record independently
insufficient_alone: Parsing isolated packets or logs without a monitoring, streaming detection, event-analysis, or incident-detection function

Training or evaluating a model once on independent rows of a static or synthetic benchmark dataset without implementing, simulating, structurally reviewing, or evaluating an operational, streaming, continuous, stateful, or correlated-event analysis function
Predicting physical defects, structural health, equipment failure, process quality, or general risk without monitoring cyber-security telemetry, compromise indicators, or malicious activity

description.definition: Extracts, structures, links, correlates, or operationally applies external threat intelligence about vulnerabilities, weaknesses, attack patterns, defensive techniques, actors, infrastructure, tactics, procedures, indicators, and relationships to risk assessment, detection, investigation, or campaign analysis
indicators: Extracting CTI entities and relations from threat reports into ontologies or knowledge graphs
Correlating indicators, TTPs and ATT&CK mapping
Correlating threat-actor or campaign attribution
Combining vulnerability, weakness, attack-pattern, and defensive-knowledge sources to assess risk or guide detection and analysis

Retrieving or deriving threat-specific reputation, indicator history, malicious infrastructure context, TTPs, or public threat records and applying them to explain or score particular alerts, flows, assets, or incidents
Automatically classifying or structuring open threat-intelligence feed records into malware, exploit, attack, actor, infrastructure, or campaign categories for threat-hunting or security decisions
insufficient_alone: Listing threat indicators or actor information without extracting, structuring, linking, or correlating threat-intelligence meaning
Citing vulnerability identifiers or threat-knowledge sources only as labels or background without applying their information to the paper's risk, detection, or analysis method
Applying generic NLP to non-CTI text without analyzing threat actors, infrastructure, TTPs, indicators, or campaigns
Adding generic protocol, location, or domain context that carries no threat-specific meaning and is not used in risk, detection, investigation, or explanation

description.definition: Detects, identifies, classifies, or analyzes malware samples, malicious payloads, malware-infected processes or memory, execution behavior, and malware-attributed network traffic to determine malicious functions, persistence, communications, indicators, or impact
indicators: Analyzing malware reverse engineering, sandboxing and unpacking
Analyzing behavior, C2 and persistence analysis
Detecting or classifying malware binaries, payloads, infected processes, memory artifacts, or encrypted malware communication and C2 traffic
Executing malware or a malware-attributed attack emulation and directly applying or evaluating containment, process, file, account, endpoint, or network response actions
Constructing or analyzing malicious documents or payload variants to measure, evade, harden, or explain malware detection behavior
insufficient_alone: Mentioning suspicious files or malware without static or dynamic analysis of their functions and impact

Detecting generic intrusions, attacks, anomalies, scans, spoofing, denial of service, or botnet activity without identifying or analyzing malware, a malicious payload, malware infection, or malware-attributed traffic

description.definition: Detects and analyzes ransomware encryption, propagation, execution, extortion, negotiation, victim impact, and response decisions, and investigates containment and recovery through memory, backups, and cryptographic weaknesses
indicators: Investigating ransomware detection, family analysis
Investigating key recovery, victim-file recovery
Analyzing victim negotiation, payment, extortion, information-leak risk, and response strategy
insufficient_alone: General malware analysis without ransomware-specific encryption, propagation, or extortion behavior

description.definition: Correlates access, copying, transfer, and exfiltration traces for documents, source code, and designs
indicators: Tracing DLP evidence, insider exfiltration and USB
Tracing email and cloud transfer, source-code similarity
insufficient_alone: General privacy or copyright investigation without analyzing access to or exfiltration of protected technology or trade secrets

description.definition: Analyzes unauthorized access, query, modification, transfer logs, and leaked data
indicators: Determining privacy breaches, personal-data exfiltration
Determining breach-scope estimation and identification of leaked information
insufficient_alone: General incident analysis without determining the affected personal data, scope, or disclosure path

description.definition: Analyzes traces of unlawful copying, modification, and distribution with platform or network records and content-identification methods
indicators: Establishing copyright forensics, content fingerprints
Establishing illegal distribution networks, piracy evidence
insufficient_alone: Checking content authenticity without analyzing unlawful copying, distribution, ownership, or infringement evidence

CVGF-02.title: Multimedia Forensics
CVGF-02.description: Analyzes the source, editing or manipulation, integrity, meaning, and distribution context of image, video, audio, and text content. It includes research on content source, authenticity, and meaning for deepfakes, copyright, image-based abuse, and disinformation. Signal and content properties are more central than generic file-structure parsing. Listed terms and cases are non-exhaustive examples; research making substantive contributions to adjacent technologies may relate to multiple categories.

description.definition: Uses sensor noise, compression or encoding parameters, metadata, and generation traces to infer or recover a media item's capture device, creation software, encoding process, compression history, or distribution provenance
indicators: Inferring camera-source identification, PRNU and codec fingerprints
Inferring acoustic environments, metadata provenance
Attributing a document or media file to creator software or software version from byte structure, encoding, or metadata traces
Recovering JPEG quantization steps or compression parameters from DCT and encoding artifacts for forensic provenance analysis
insufficient_alone: Detecting manipulation without inferring the capture device, creation tool, or distribution path

CVGF-02-02.title: Media Tampering Detection and Integrity Verification

description.definition: Examines discontinuities in pixels, frames, audio, and metadata and verifies hashes, signatures, or content credentials to detect editing and synthesis
indicators: Detecting image, video and audio forgery detection and deepfakes
Detecting splicing, copy-move and recompression
insufficient_alone: Inferring a generating device or tool without testing the media for editing, synthesis, or integrity anomalies
Generating adversarial or anti-forensic media that defeats an existing detector without implementing detection or integrity verification of the manipulated content

description.definition: Jointly analyzes video, audio, images, and text to assess semantic, temporal, speaker, and scene consistency and case relevance across modalities
indicators: Assessing vision-language, audio-visual and text-image consistency
Assessing speaker-lip synchronization and cross-modal meaning
insufficient_alone: Detecting forgery in one medium without analyzing consistency across image, video, audio, or text modalities

CVGF-03.title: Virtual Asset (Cryptocurrency) Forensics
CVGF-03.description: Combines on-chain records with off-chain wallet, exchange, and service data to determine cryptocurrency movement, concealment, exchange, cash-out paths, and actors. It includes investigative tracing and attribution for cryptocurrency crime, laundering, fraud, and illicit payment. General blockchain performance or security without an evidentiary purpose is outside the core scope. Listed terms and cases are non-exhaustive examples; research making substantive contributions to adjacent technologies may relate to multiple categories.

description.definition: Analyzes transaction inputs and outputs, token transfers, smart-contract interactions, and address relationships
indicators: Tracing transaction graphs, address clustering and fund-flow tracing
Tracing smart-contract events and token transfers
insufficient_alone: Reconstructing only mixer or evasion behavior without tracing ordinary inputs, outputs, transfers, and address relationships

description.definition: Reconstructs flows obscured by mixers, chain hopping, privacy mechanisms, and distributed transfers using time, value, pattern, and cross-chain correlation
indicators: Reconstructing mixers, tumblers and chain hopping
Reconstructing peel chains, privacy coins and bridges
insufficient_alone: Ordinary on-chain tracing without mixers, chain hopping, privacy mechanisms, or another deliberate obfuscation structure

description.definition: Analyzes exchange deposits and withdrawals, wallet apps, payment services, authentication, device, and network logs
indicators: Linking addresses with exchange KYC and wallet artifacts
Correlating account, IP, device, and payment records
insufficient_alone: Using only blockchain-ledger data without linking addresses to exchange, wallet, authentication, device, or network records

CVGF-04.title: Industry and Specialized Domain Forensics
CVGF-04.description: Analyzes devices, sensors, control commands, operational logs, and communications in industrial and specialized environments to determine incidents, malfunctions, and intrusions. It includes research that jointly interprets digital records and physical behavior in cyber-physical systems. Device-specific protocols, safety, operational context, and domain knowledge distinguish it from general computer forensics. Listed terms and cases are non-exhaustive examples; research making substantive contributions to adjacent technologies may relate to multiple categories.

description.definition: Analyzes location, trajectory, sensor, control, operation, and communication records from drones, vehicles, and vessels
indicators: Reconstructing drone flight logs, vehicle EDR and IVI and CAN
Reconstructing vessel VDR, AIS and ECDIS and GPS or sensor fusion for accident reconstruction
insufficient_alone: Analyzing aircraft or satellite records without examining drone, vehicle, or vessel operation

description.definition: Analyzes control records, sensor data, work histories, and environmental perception from service, industrial, and autonomous robots
indicators: Reconstructing robot control logs, ROS artifacts and autonomy stacks
Reconstructing actuators, sensors and task histories
insufficient_alone: Analyzing vehicle or drone movement without examining robot control, sensing, task history, or malfunction

description.definition: Analyzes medical devices, biosignal equipment, hospital systems, and telemedicine records
indicators: Investigating medical-device logs, EHR and wearables
Investigating biosignals, PACS and telemedicine
insufficient_alone: General privacy-breach analysis without a medical-device, clinical-care, or hospital-system context

description.definition: Collects, preserves, or analyzes digital evidence from ICS, SCADA, industrial control devices, and smart factories, including device images, memory, commands, state changes, process data, logs, and network records
indicators: Acquiring or preserving memory, disk images, logs, or configurations from ICS devices
Reconstructing PLC, HMI and historians
Reconstructing SCADA logs, industrial protocols and process state
Implementing isolation or forensic collection and analysis specifically for compromised industrial systems
insufficient_alone: Analyzing general enterprise IT logs without examining industrial commands, process states, sensors, or actuators

description.definition: Analyzes operational, sensor, and communication records from aircraft, satellites, ground stations, and navigation equipment
indicators: Reconstructing aircraft flight data, avionics
Reconstructing ground stations, GNSS spoofing
insufficient_alone: Analyzing drone, vehicle, or vessel records without examining aircraft, satellite, ground-station, or navigation evidence

CVGF-05.title: Artificial Intelligence Forensics
CVGF-05.description: Uses AI to automate forensic analysis while also treating AI models, operational environments, and generated content as evidence subjects. It includes both AI used as a forensic tool and AI systems or outputs treated as evidence, separated into three subcategories. General AI performance research must be directly connected to evidence analysis, attribution, or verification. Listed terms and cases are non-exhaustive examples; research making substantive contributions to adjacent technologies may relate to multiple categories.

description.definition: Uses AI to automate digital-forensic evidence or artifact preparation, classification, correlation, anomaly or malware analysis, prioritization, and reporting support, narrowing material for forensic examiner or incident-investigation review
indicators: Automating machine-learning evidence triage, artifact classification
Automating timeline generation, agentic forensics
Classifying malware from binaries, memory dumps, network traces, or other forensic artifacts
Automating forensic media authenticity, provenance, or encoding-parameter analysis and prioritizing questioned media for examiner review
Using AI to extract or quality-control incident indicators from exploits, artifacts, or threat records for post-incident analysis
insufficient_alone: Investigating an AI model without using AI to automate evidence preparation, classification, correlation, or prioritization

Applying machine learning to general intrusion detection, security monitoring, vulnerability prediction, software quality, or network classification without a digital-forensic evidence-analysis or incident-investigation function

Using deterministic hashing, string comparison, similarity, graph drawing, clustering, or visualization alone without a learned or reasoning AI method performing a defined forensic analysis or narrowing evidence for examiner review

description.definition: Analyzes data provenance, model versions, prompts, inference logs, configuration changes, and external integrations across development, training, deployment, and operation
indicators: Reconstructing AI-model forensics, training-data provenance
Reconstructing model extraction, poisoning and prompt injection
insufficient_alone: Detecting only whether final content is synthetic without examining AI-system data provenance, model versions, prompts, inference logs, or configuration changes

Using, training, testing, explaining, attacking, or validating an AI model as the paper's analytical or security method without investigating the AI system itself as an evidence source or incident target

CVGF-05-03.title: AI-generated Content Identification and Abuse Response

description.definition: Analyzes generation artifacts, watermarks, model traits, and distribution paths in synthetic image, video, audio, and text
indicators: Detecting synthetic image, audio, video, or text
Attributing generated content with fingerprints or watermarks
insufficient_alone: Analyzing internal AI-service logs without identifying generated content or tracing its attribution, distribution, or abuse
